abase|chagrin.distinction: Abase is the act of humbling someone, usually oneself, while chagrin is the sting of humiliation felt afterwards.

abase|humble.distinction: Abase degrades someone to a shameful level, while humble only lowers their pride or rank and can be well deserved.

abase|humiliate.distinction: Abase is lowering someone in dignity, often oneself deliberately, while humiliate is inflicting shame on another person.

abase|mortify.distinction: Abase is degrading someone in standing, while mortify is the burning embarrassment felt by the person it happens to.

abdicate|renounce.distinction: Abdicate gives up an office or duty you hold, while renounce gives up any claim, belief or title, formally and in public.

aberration|deviance.distinction: An aberration is a one-off departure from the normal, while deviance is a settled pattern of breaking accepted standards.

abhor|execrate.distinction: Abhor is hating something deeply and often privately, while execrate is cursing it aloud for everyone to hear.

abhor|loathe.distinction: Abhor carries moral disgust at something wrong, while loathe is intense personal hatred needing no principle behind it.

abide|brook.distinction: Abide can mean to endure or to stay put, while brook only ever means to tolerate, and almost always in the negative.

abject|scurvy.distinction: Abject is wretched and stripped of all dignity, while scurvy is contemptible in a mean and shabby way.

abjure|forswear.distinction: Abjure is renouncing under oath and in public, while forswear is swearing something off for yourself.

abjure|recant.distinction: Abjure renounces a claim or practice on oath, while recant withdraws a belief you had previously stated as true.

abjure|retract.distinction: Abjure is a solemn renunciation on oath, while retract simply takes back something said, with no ceremony at all.

abstain|forbear.distinction: Abstain is going without as a settled practice, while forbear is holding back this once when you could have acted.

abstruse|esoteric.distinction: Abstruse is hard for anyone to follow, while esoteric is plain enough inside the small circle that shares the knowledge.

abstruse|recondite.distinction: Abstruse is difficult because the reasoning runs deep, while recondite is obscure because so few people study the subject.

accede|acquiesce.distinction: Accede is agreeing to a demand, willingly or not, while acquiesce is going along in silence without ever really agreeing.

accede|assent.distinction: Accede is yielding to a demand or joining a treaty, while assent is simply giving your approval to a proposal.

accede|defer.distinction: Accede grants what was asked, while defer stands back and lets someone else's judgment settle the matter.

acclaim|hail.distinction: Acclaim is the praise a public gives, while hail is the act of calling someone out as something great.

acerbic|acrid.distinction: Acerbic is sharpness of tone in what someone says, while acrid is a smell or taste that bites the nose and throat.

acerbic|astringent.distinction: Acerbic wit is bitter and meant to wound, while astringent criticism is severe but bracing, the way alum tightens skin.

acerbic|caustic.distinction: Acerbic is sour and cutting in tone, while caustic burns: it is the stronger word and it is meant to do damage.

acme|apex.distinction: Acme is the highest point of quality or achievement, while apex is the geometric tip or the top of a structure.

acme|pinnacle.distinction: Acme is the peak of excellence in a field, while pinnacle is the height of a career or a literal spire.

acme|summit.distinction: Acme is the highest standard a thing can reach, while summit is the top of a mountain or a meeting of leaders.

acrid|caustic.distinction: Acrid is a bitter smell or taste that stings, while caustic is corrosive, whether chemically or in what someone says.

acrimony|jaundice.distinction: Acrimony is bitterness in how people speak to each other, while jaundice is the soured outlook colouring what someone sees.

acumen|perspicacity.distinction: Acumen is shrewd practical judgment, especially in business, while perspicacity is seeing through to what others miss.

adamant|inexorable.distinction: Adamant is a person refusing to be moved, while inexorable is a process no amount of pleading can stop.

adamant|intransigent.distinction: Adamant is firm on one point and can be admired, while intransigent refuses every compromise and rarely is.

adept|proficient.distinction: Adept is real flair at something, while proficient is competence: a proficient pianist plays correctly, an adept one plays well.

adhere|cleave.distinction: Adhere is sticking to a surface or a rule, while cleave famously means both to split apart and to cling fast.

adhere|cohere.distinction: Adhere is one thing sticking to another, while cohere is the parts of a single thing holding together.

adjudicate|resolve.distinction: Adjudicate is a judge formally settling a dispute, while resolve is the firm determination someone brings to a decision.

adjure|beseech.distinction: Adjure is charging someone solemnly, as if on oath, while beseech is begging from a position of no power at all.

adjure|conjure.distinction: Adjure is urging someone earnestly to act, while conjure is summoning something up as if by magic.

adjure|entreat.distinction: Adjure carries the weight of a solemn charge, while entreat is humble earnest asking with no authority behind it.

adulterate|debase.distinction: Adulterate weakens a substance by mixing something inferior into it, while debase lowers the worth or dignity of anything.

adverse|untoward.distinction: Adverse conditions work against you, while untoward events are unexpected and improper rather than simply unfavourable.

advocate|exponent.distinction: An advocate argues for a cause, while an exponent also practises it and is usually its leading example.

advocate|proponent.distinction: Advocate suggests active public campaigning, while a proponent is whoever puts a proposal forward and backs it.

affable|amiable.distinction: Affable is being easy to fall into conversation with, while amiable is a pleasant nature whether or not anyone speaks.

affable|cordial.distinction: Affable is being easy to talk to, while cordial is warmth shown deliberately, often within formal politeness.

affable|genial.distinction: Affable is approachable in conversation, while genial is cheerful warmth that lifts the mood of a whole room.

affect|feign.distinction: Affect is putting on a manner you want believed, while feign is faking a state you do not have, such as illness.

affluent|flush.distinction: Affluent is settled long-term wealth, while flush is having plenty of money at this particular moment.

aggrandize|embellish.distinction: Aggrandize inflates power or importance, while embellish adds decoration or invented detail to a story.

aggravate|exacerbate.distinction: Aggravate can mean to annoy a person as well as to worsen a problem, while exacerbate only ever worsens a situation.

aggravate|exasperate.distinction: Aggravate worsens a condition, while exasperate wears out a person's patience until they lose their temper.

allay|assuage.distinction: Allay settles fear or doubt, while assuage soothes any strong feeling, including grief, hunger and anger.

allay|slake.distinction: Allay calms a fear or a suspicion, while slake satisfies a physical craving, above all thirst.

allege|aver.distinction: Allege asserts something without offering proof, while aver states it confidently as fact and stands behind it.

alleviate|assuage.distinction: Alleviate lessens pain or hardship, while assuage soothes feelings, so you alleviate poverty but assuage grief.

alleviate|palliate.distinction: Alleviate genuinely reduces the trouble, while palliate eases the symptoms and leaves the cause untouched.

ameliorate|amend.distinction: Ameliorate makes a bad situation better, while amend alters a text or a law, whether or not it improves anything.

amend|emend.distinction: Amend changes a law or document, often by adding to it, while emend corrects errors in a text and nothing else.

amiable|cordial.distinction: Amiable is a pleasant nature someone simply has, while cordial is warmth actively offered to a guest or a rival.

amiable|genial.distinction: Amiable is good-natured and easy, while genial is actively cheerful and makes the people around it cheerful too.

analgesic|anodyne.distinction: An analgesic is a drug that kills pain, while anodyne now usually means remarks so bland they could offend nobody.

ancillary|appurtenant.distinction: Ancillary work supports the main task, while appurtenant is a legal word for what attaches to a property or a right.

ancillary|auxiliary.distinction: Ancillary is subordinate and supporting, while auxiliary is extra capacity held in reserve, like an auxiliary engine.

animosity|animus.distinction: Animosity is open hostility between people, while animus is the hidden motive of ill will behind an action.

annul|countermand.distinction: Annul cancels something so it is treated as never valid, while countermand reverses an order already given.

annul|nullify.distinction: Annul is the formal legal voiding of a thing such as a marriage, while nullify is anything that robs it of effect.

annul|quash.distinction: Annul voids a thing from the start, while quash puts down a verdict, a rebellion or a rumour that already exists.

annul|repeal.distinction: Annul voids a particular act or contract, while repeal removes a whole law from the statute book.

annul|rescind.distinction: Annul declares that something never validly existed, while rescind withdraws a decision or offer that did.

antecedent|precursor.distinction: An antecedent simply came earlier, while a precursor led to what followed and helped bring it about.

antecedent|predecessor.distinction: An antecedent is any earlier thing or cause, while a predecessor is the person who held your post before you.

antedated|preceded.distinction: Antedated means dated earlier than the true date, or existing before, while preceded simply means came first in order.

antipathy|aversion.distinction: Antipathy is settled dislike of a person or an idea, while aversion is the urge to keep away from what repels you.

antiquated|archaic.distinction: Antiquated means outdated and no longer fit for use, while archaic belongs to a much older period of the language.

apathy|indifference.distinction: Apathy is having no feeling left at all, often through exhaustion, while indifference is simply not caring either way.

apex|summit.distinction: Apex is the pointed top of a shape or a career, while summit is a mountain top or a meeting of heads of state.

aphorism|apothegm.distinction: An aphorism states a general truth with polish, while an apothegm is terser and meant to instruct.

aplomb|poise.distinction: Aplomb is visible confidence in a tricky moment, while poise is the steady composure that never wobbles in the first place.

apostate|renegade.distinction: An apostate abandons a faith or doctrine, while a renegade abandons a side and often joins the other one.

apotheosis|paragon.distinction: Apotheosis is being raised to the highest form of a thing, while a paragon is simply a perfect example of a quality.

apparent|evident.distinction: Apparent can mean seeming rather than real, while evident always means plainly true on the face of it.

apparent|manifest.distinction: Apparent leaves room for doubt about what only seems so, while manifest is obvious beyond any argument.

apparent|palpable.distinction: Apparent is what can be seen or supposed, while palpable is a tension or relief so strong it feels almost physical.

apparent|patent.distinction: Apparent may be appearance only, while patent is openly and undeniably the case, as in patent nonsense.

appease|assuage.distinction: Appease buys off an angry party by giving in, while assuage soothes a feeling without conceding anything at all.

appease|conciliate.distinction: Appease yields to demands to avoid trouble, while conciliate wins the other side over and ends the quarrel.

appease|mollify.distinction: Appease concedes something to stop a threat, while mollify only softens the temper of someone already angry.

appease|pacify.distinction: Appease buys peace with concessions, while pacify restores calm, sometimes by force, as an army pacifies a region.

appease|placate.distinction: Appease gives ground to an aggressor, while placate calms an offended person, often with an apology rather than a concession.

diabolic|diabolical.distinction: Diabolic and diabolical mean the same thing, and diabolical is much the commoner form in ordinary use.

elude|evade.distinction: Elude is slipping out of reach, including out of memory, while evade is dodging something you are supposed to face.

endow|endue.distinction: Endow can give money as well as a quality, while endue is the older word and grants only a quality, never a fund.

lambast|lambaste.distinction: Lambast and lambaste are the same verb, and lambaste is the spelling most dictionaries list first.

largess|largesse.distinction: Largess and largesse are one word, and largesse keeps the French ending that British writing prefers.

nonplused|nonplussed.distinction: Nonplused and nonplussed are the same word, and nonplussed with two s is the standard spelling.

optimal|optimum.distinction: Optimal is the adjective for the best setting available, while optimum is usually the noun naming that best point itself.

oscillate|vacillate.distinction: Oscillate is swinging back and forth, in physics or in mood, while vacillate is a person failing to settle on a choice.

pre-empt|preempt.distinction: Pre-empt and preempt are one verb, and the hyphen is only convention: British writing keeps it, American writing drops it.

raffish|rakish.distinction: Raffish is disreputable in a shabby bohemian way, while rakish is disreputable with dash and a tilt of the hat.

rebut|refute.distinction: Rebut is answering an argument, while refute is succeeding at it: a refuted claim has been disproved, a rebutted one only answered.

stanch|staunch.distinction: Stanch is the verb for stopping a flow of blood or of losses, while staunch is the adjective for someone firmly loyal.
